{{user}} decided to spend time with his friends, the orc girl Sophia and the goblin girl Lola. They strolled around the mall, enjoying the atmosphere of shopping and fun. The shops were brightly lit, and the smell of freshly baked goods from the cafe hung in the air. {{user}} felt relaxed and happy in the company of the girls, because their friendship was always full of laughter and adventure.

When they approached the clothing store, Lola exclaimed with delight: "Let's go in! I heard they are having a sale!" Sophia, with her strong character and cheerful nature, nodded: "Yes, let's! I want to see the new collections!" {{user}} could not resist their enthusiasm and agreed.

Inside the store, the atmosphere was shopping: the girls were sorting through things, discussing what suits them and what does not. {{user}}, watching their excitement, noticed a door marked "Staff". A playful thought popped into his head: "Why not take a look in there?" A voice inside him told him that this could be a fun adventure.

Sophia, winking at {{user}}, said with a smile: "You know this is not for us, but I like your adventurous spirit!" Lola, with her mischievous and slightly cheeky mood, added: "Come on, this will be fun! We are breaking the law of fashion!"

They entered the staff room, where there were boxes of clothes, old mannequins and a few unsorted goods. It was quiet inside, and the girls began to joke about how they became "villains" hiding from security. "Soon we will be on the news as the most stylish criminals!" Lola laughed, trying on one of the old hats.

However, when they decided to go back to the store, {{user}} pulled the door handle, but it did not budge. "Hey, what the fuck?" he asked in surprise, pulling the handle again. Sophia came closer and tried to help, but the door remained closed. Lola, noticing the confusion on her friends' faces, got a little scared and shouted: "Fuck! What the fuck!? Someone let us out of here." But there was no answer. They all realized that they were stuck here for a long time.

entries.name: -----Playable Races-----
entries.content: Below is all things racially related

entries.name: Dragonborn
entries.content:
A proud race that values clan and skills above all else. Once enslaved by dragons, they strive to be self-sufficient, not wanting to be beholden to anyone, not even the gods.

They have resistance to a type of energy damage, and are able to make deadly breath attacks. These abilities are affected by their dragonborn subrace. 
Dragonborn resemble draconic humanoids, can have scales in a variety of colours, and may or may not have a tail.

entries.name: Drow (Lolth-Sworn)
entries.content:
Driven to the Underdark, most drow have adopted a ruthless pragmatism. The Lolth-sworn delight in the goddess' evil tenets.

Often shades of blue grey with pointed ears, the Lolth-sworn drow are cruel, violent but beautiful sub-race of elves.
All Lolth-sworn drow have red colored eyes - a sign of where their loyalties lie.

entries.name: Drow (Seldarine)
entries.content:
Seldarine drow can be found seeking allies from all over Faerûn, aiming to settle their conflict with Lolth - and each other - by any means necessary.

Seldarine drow are a much more peaceful sect of the drowish culture, they follow the example of their goddess - Eilistraee and strive to align with the forces of good.

The Seldarine's still have the beauty and appearances of their Lolth-Sworn counterparts, However they are not born with red eyes.

entries.name: Dwarf (Duergar)
entries.content:
Once enslaved by the eldritch mind flayers, duergar adapted to freedom with harsh practicality. Their cold demeanours and gift of stealth are well-known throughout the Underdark. 

They have the appearance of a stocky dwarf, however, their skin is always a grey-black and due to their home being the underdark, they are very sensitive to the sunlight.

Alcohol can cause Duergar to have visions of ancestral torment at the hands of the mind flayers.

entries.name: Dwarf (Gold)
entries.content:
These dwarves are known for their confidence and keen intuition. The culture of their Deep Kingdom values family, ritual, and fine craftsmanship.

This Dwarven subrace is known for it's craftmanship, they are often what one might think of when dwarves come into mind.

They have the average appearance of a dwarf, Short, stocky, their men often have very large and well cared for beards.

entries.name: Dwarf (Shield)
entries.content:
Great losses in ancient wars against goblins and orcs have led these dwarves to adopt a cynical mindset, but they will endure anything to restore their ancestral homelands.

This sub-race of Dwarf is hearty and stubborn, Often time able to take a beating and well trained with armors.

They have the average appearance of a dwarf, Short, stocky, their men often have very large and well cared for beards.

entries.name: Elf (High)
entries.content:
Heirs of the mystical Feywild, high elves value magic in all its forms, and even those who do not study spellcraft can manipulate the Weave. 

The High-elf subrace of elves are natural magicians often times making great mages. They are long lived, and have an affinity for magic.

Most Elves have an ethereal beauty about them and high elves are no acceptation. They look as if they were just extremely beautiful humans, the only thing that sets them apart is their long pointed ears.

entries.name: Elf (Wood)
entries.content:
With ethereal countenances and long lifespans, elves are at home with nature's power, flourishing in light and dark alike. These elves spend their reclusive lives in Faerûn's forests. Decades of training in archery and camouflage are enhanced by an otherworldly swiftness.

The wood elf is a sub-race of elves that are second to none in matters of archery. They are master archers and hunters thanks to their natural perception, sharp hearing and uncanny speeds through the forest.

The look much like other elves, however have more of a naturally yellow hue to their skin.

entries.name: Githyanki
entries.content:
Githyanki are peerless warriors from the Astral Plane, known for their legendary silver blades and red dragon mounts. They seek the total destruction of mind flayers, whose ancient empire enslaved the ancestral gith for millennia.

As the effects of time is diminished in their native Astral Plane, githyanki are instead hatched from eggs all across realmspace in places called crèches. Crèches act as hatcheries, training grounds, and shelters outside of the Astral Plane.

The Githyanki are naturally very xenophobic and supremacist, believing themselves to be the perfect warrior race.

The Githyanki are very alien appearing compared to other humanoid races, often being long, lanky, green and lack a nose, only having nostrils and their pupils are vertical slits.

entries.name: Gnome (Deep)
entries.content:
Small, clever, and energetic, gnomes use their long lives to explore Faerûn's brightest corners and darkest depths. However, More guarded than their surface cousins, deep gnomes survive in the Underdark with darkvision and skillful stealth.

Deep gnomes are often hunted down for sport by Lolth-sworn drown, or enslaved by the Duergar. They lives are often just a fight to survive in the cruel underdark.

Deep gnomes are one of the smallest races in Faerûn's, coming in smaller than dwarves, they are somewhat lanky, But much like all underdark residents, their skin is naturally dark and their hair white.

entries.name: Gnome (Forest)
entries.content:
Small, clever, and energetic, gnomes use their long lives to explore Faerûn's brightest corners and darkest depths. Even smaller than their cousins and twice as reclusive, forest gnomes are a rare sight in Faerûn. They master magic and craftsmanship in their distant, idyllic groves.

The Forest Gnomes prefer to stay in their forest, due to their link with nature, they have the natural ability to cast magic so they might speak with animals. 

They appear to be even smaller than the average Gnome and naturally have a yellow/brown skin tone.

entries.name: Gnome (Rock)
entries.content:
Small, clever, and energetic, gnomes use their long lives to explore Faerûn's brightest corners and darkest depths. This sub-race of gnome are the most commonly seen gnomes on Faerûn's surface, rock gnomes are named as such for their hardiness and affinity for metal.

Due to their size and affinity with metals as well as their handiness, they are natural fine craftsmen, often praised for their metal and stone work.

They appear to be a mixed bag Gnomish traits, sharing traits with both of their Gnomish cousin races.

entries.name: Half-Elf (Drow)
entries.content:
Most half-drow result from liaisons between Seldarine drow and surfacers. While half-drow inherited a few magical gifts, they aren't usually raised in the Underdark.

A half-drow still contains some magical prowess of their drowish parent, their blood is diluted by simpleness of a humans, loosing their haunting beauty, however still looking very attractive by human standards.

entries.name: Half-Elf (High)
entries.content:
A touch of the Feywild remains in half-elves with this bloodline, and even those untrained in magic possess a hint of wild power.

Like all half bloods, they gain the benefit of some of their elven parent's prowess, however is is diluted by the human blood that flows through them. Making Half-High elf's decent mages, however it can be wild and untamed without guidance.

They also lose their etheric beauty but still remain beautiful by human standards.

entries.name: Half-Elf (Wood)
entries.content:
Like their wood elf parent, these half-elves have a quickened stride and an eye for stealth. Yet many break away from isolation in Faerûn's forests to explore the rest of the Realms.

The half-wood elves are always natural hunters, not as good as full blooded wood elves, but they are able to achieve athletic speeds and are naturals with stealth

entries.name: Halfling (Lightfoot)
entries.content:
Small yet capable, halflings prefer the comforts of home and hearth - but their natural luck and dexterity makes them fine adventurers. Stealthy but social, these halflings travel all over Faerûn to make names for themselves.

Often times these short charismatic creatures are renown bards due to their natural gift of the gab and their...roguish behaviors, they're able to charm their way out of many things, not to mention their natural luck.

They appear as small humanoids, smaller than dwarves, taller than gnomes.

entries.name: Halfling (Strongheart)
entries.content:
Small yet capable, halflings prefer the comforts of home and hearth - but their natural luck and dexterity makes them fine adventurers. Legend has it that dwarven blood gave stronghearts their hardiness. Resistant to poison and wellsprings of endurance, these halflings easily hold their own.

Resistant to poison and sturdy to boot, these potential half bloods of halflings and Dwarf-kind are small but fierce, not the best warriors by a long shot, however, in terms of halflings, they are mighty.

They appear to be short humanoids, Shorter than dwarfs, taller than gnomes.

entries.name: Half-Orc
entries.content:
They are born of both human and orc ancestry, and exhibit a blend of orcish and human characteristics, their appearances varying widely. Creatures of intense emotion, half-orcs are more inclined to act than contemplate - whether the rage burning their bodies compels them to fight, or the love filling their hearts inspires acts of incredible kindness.

Half orcs are naturally fierce melee warriors, due to their Orcish ancestry but they aren't savage brutes due to the tempering of human blood. 

They appear to be one of the tallest races in Faerun, almost always sporting green skin and tusk, they are far from beautiful by average human standards, often even looking off putting in most cases.

entries.name: Human
entries.content:
They are one of the most populous races in Faerûn, exhibiting a versatile range of skills rather than any one mastery. The most common face in Faerûn, humans are known for their tenacity, creativity, and endless capacity for growth.

Humans seem to have the the ability to breed with most races and produce offspring, making them valuable in their own right.

entries.name: Tiefling (Asmodeus)
entries.content:
Touched by the Hells, Tieflings are resistant to fire and carry extraordinary Infernal powers. Descended from devils of the Nine Hells, Tieflings face constant suspicion in Faerûn. Thankfully, their arcane abilities make them natural survivors.

Bound to Nessus, the deepest layer of the Hells, these Tieflings inherited the ability to wield fire and darkness from the archdevil Asmodeus' infernal bloodline.

This subrace of Tieflings often have devilishly red skin and the horns of a devil, though they are anything but.

entries.name: Tiefling (Mephistopheles)
entries.content:
Descended from devils of the Nine Hells, Tieflings face constant suspicion in Faerûn. Thankfully, their arcane abilities make them natural survivors. Descended from the archdevil Mephistopheles, these Tieflings are gifted with a particular affinity for arcane magic.

Mephistopheles Tieflings are naturally magically gifted, making them their races mages often times.

They have the appearance of Blueish grey skin with purple glowing eyes and devilish horns.

entries.name: Tiefling (Zariel)
entries.content:
Descended from devils of the Nine Hells, Tieflings face constant suspicion in Faerûn. Thankfully, their arcane abilities make them natural survivors. Tieflings from Zariel's bloodline are empowered with martial strength, and can channel searing flame to punish their enemies.

Due to their bloodline, this sub-race of Tieflings make for natural warriors, due to their blood wars in Avernus, These Tieflings can be terrifying in battle.

They appear to have yellow skin with glowing red eyes and devilish horns.

entries.name: Aasimar
entries.content: Endowed with a divine lineage, aasimar represent the physical and mental experience of other mortal creatures elevated. In the long uncertain night of Faerûnian life, they burn like pale inspiring torches. Similar to Tieflings, Aasimar are creatures either descended from or touched by celestials or other good-aligned beings.

entries.name: Bugbear
entries.content: They are hairy goblinoids that thrive in battle and are fond of raiding, hunting, and ambushing. Bugbears are often fighting alongside goblins and other members of the Cult of the Absolute. These hairy humanoids crave carnage and treasure in equal measure, using a mix of brute force and guile to get what they want.

entries.name: Cambion
entries.content: Typically found in the Hells, Cambions are half-fiend, half-mortal, and are resistant to many types of damage. Scarlet-eyed and bitter-tempered, cambion are the bastard children of devils and mortals, a fusion of two Planes in one body.

entries.name: Deva
entries.content: Devas are a type of Celestial creature. They can be summoned to a spellcaster's aid. They appear to be humans with wings.

entries.name: Djinni
entries.content: Djinn are a type of Elemental creature. They can be summoned to a spellcaster's aid that have the appearance of a typical Genie.

entries.name: Drider
entries.content: Favoured drow that fail the tests of the Webmother Lolth have their forms warped and made wicked - grafted with spiders to serve as symbols of her power. Drider are centaur-like creatures that appear to have the upper body of a Drow, with the lower half replaced by a giant spider.

entries.name: Dryad
entries.content: Dryads are mysterious Fey race, They channel powerful druidic powers, allowing them to entangle their enemies and call forth Wood Woads for help. They are also unnaturally beautiful and very revealing of their bodies.

entries.name: Githzerai
entries.content: Githzerai are an ascetic splinter group of gith that now live in the Limbo Plane, after millennia of enslavement by mind flayers.

entries.name: Goblin
entries.content: Weak, selfish humanoids. Though they often serve stronger races, they crave power and abuse what authority they obtain. Goblins are small-sized. This might be an advantage for places with holes and tunnels, which they can squeeze through to ambush their enemies. They usually have low weight, which means they are easier to throw and push than most creatures. Goblin skin is usually wrinkled and their skin tones are a range of yellow, brown, and/or green, and some may have slurred speech.

entries.name: Hag
entries.content:
Hags are a notorious Fey Race. They are clever, highly magical creatures who delight in the suffering they cause. Their power is further increased by their collections of magical trinkets, created by the Hag over the years. 

According to The Evil Eye book, there are three known kinds of hags: Green Hags, Sea Hags, and Night Hags. Night Hags are named after their ability to haunt a mortal's dreams. They slowly devour the mortal's vital essence, collecting it in their soul bag. They are known to be petty and selfish, and prone to bragging. Sea Hags are said to smell of fish, and prefer to eat their victims whole. They can kill with a glance. Green Hags can appear as beautiful mortals, are very dangerous, and are quick to anger.

entries.name: Harpy
entries.content: Sadistic creatures with the legs and wings of a vulture and the body of an elf. Their sweet song enchants their prey, luring them to their deaths.

entries.name: Hobgoblin
entries.content: Large, brutal humanoids that live for martial prowess, war, and glory. Hobgoblins resemble larger Goblins with dark orange or red-orange skin. Hobgoblins typically prize strength and martial prowess, and value skill and cunning in battle.

entries.name: Hollyphant
entries.content: Hollyphants are celestial creatures, They closely resemble miniature elephants with golden fur and wings Bobbing like corks in the earnest, busy muddle-puddle of their lives, hollyphants are sweet-natured little pachyderms who often serve as helpers to good-aligned deities

entries.name: Incubus
entries.content:
The fiend male counterpart to a succubus, though they are interchangeable. 
Sensual and depraved, these dark-winged fiends from the Nine Hells derive pleasure from enticing and devouring lonely souls. Incubi are lusty, and seductive creatures that ultimately aim to slay mortals and take their souls. They accomplish this by using their shape changing powers to assume a form that most humanoids find extremely attractive. They are cunning linguists, and frequently charm their victims.

entries.name: Kobold
entries.content: Clever but craven reptilians that overcome their physical ineptitude by banding together. Kobolds resemble small scaley lizards that stand upright. They can also speak very simple common tongue and revere Dragonborns as gods due to having the blood of a dragon in them.

entries.name: Kuo-toa
entries.content:
They are degenerate and sadistic amphibian humanoids, but they can generally be communicated with. Mad, fish-like denizens of the Underdark. They revere imaginary gods with an insane religious fervour.

Once inhabiting the shores and islands of the surface world, Kuo-toa now dwell in the Underdark. They are generally cruel and sadistic creatures with a cunning intelligence and have the appearance of fish-like humanoids. Kuo-toa are former mind flayer slaves that have the power to manifest their gods through their own belief.

entries.name: Mind flayers
entries.content:
Psionic tyrants, slavers, and interdimensional voyagers that feed off the brains of thinking creatures.

Mind flayers are psionic aberrations with a humanoid-like figure and a tentacled head that communicate using telepathy. They feast on the brains of intelligent beings and can enthrall other creatures to their will. Every mind flayer is connected to an Elder Brain, a colossal and powerful psionic brain that commands the mind flayers it is linked to.

Mind flayers reproduce by infecting other creatures with a tadpole that consumes its host from the inside, transforming them into another mind flayer in a process called  ceremorphosis.

Thousands of years ago, mind flayers were a dominant planar power. Using massive flying vessels called Nautiloids, they traveled to hundreds of worlds, harvesting intelligent humanoids to consume, propagate their race, and use as slave labour. One of their enslaved races, the gith, rose up and destroyed their empire, leaving only small pockets of mind flayers behind.

entries.name: Minotaur
entries.content: Minotaurs are large humanoid creatures with bull heads and savage roars. They are known for being able to recall any path they have previously traveled. Minotaurs are native to the Underdark.

entries.name: Mummy (race)
entries.content: Shambling, their bodies clothed with rotted scraps of funereal wrappings, mummies bring their malice with them out of their tombs.

entries.name: Myconid
entries.content:
Myconids are a peaceful species of sentient fungi found in the Underdark. Groups of myconids live in communities called circles – a collective consciousness or hivemind that communicate through a song-like telepathy, speaking in visions and music. Other species may communicate with myconids through the ingestion of airborn spores.

Circles are lead by a single Sovereign, who determines the song of its people (and thus the temperament of a circle), and is able to spawn more myconid by embedding spores into a corpse and resurrecting it.

As the Underdark lacks in food sources or light, myconid have evolved to sustain themselves by drinking the essence of the energy of the Underdark. As such, myconid cannot leave the Underdark.

entries.name: Ogre
entries.content: Ogres are known for their strength and short tempers. As stupid as they are gluttonous, these hulking giants are known for their quick tempers. They live by raiding, scavenging, and killing for food and pleasure both

entries.name: Pixie
entries.content: Pixies are a tiny Fey creature, infamous for their trickery, which is sometimes playful and sometimes malicious. They enjoy playing pranks, but some also perform more helpful magic.

entries.name: Redcap
entries.content: Small, homicidal creatures. Born of bloodlust, they have to keep their caps steeped in blood to survive. These Fey creatures Known for their bloodlust, they almost exclusively appear in the Sunlit Wetlands, although some also make an appearance in Rivington and the Lower City.

entries.name: Shadar-Kai
entries.content: These elves were transformed by the Shadowfell, until nothing remained but a mournful, joyless existence between life and death. Shadar-kai serve the Raven Queen inside the Shadowfell. They were formerly elves before being trapped in the Shadowfell and transformed. The Raven Queen, who is obsessed with collecting memories and essences (typically of loss and grief), sends the shadar-kai to retrieve mementos of tragic events, whether they are physical tokens, memories, or the souls of the dead.

entries.name: Succubus
entries.content: The male version are called an Incubus, though they are able to freely change genders at will Native to the Lower Planes, succubi beckon those they seduce with soft fingers, concealing their claws beneath. Succubus are lusty, and seductive creatures that ultimately aim to slay mortals and take their souls. They accomplish this by using their shape changing powers to assume a form that most humanoids find extremely attractive. They are cunning linguists, and frequently charm their victims.

entries.name: Werewolf
entries.content:
Savage predators that spread their curse through biting other humanoids.

Most werewolves succumb to their bloodlust, but some learn to control their urges, often under the guidance of Selûne, goddess of the moon. Werewolves have the incredibly rare distinction of being immune to non-magical bludgeoning, slashing, and piercing damage. This makes them dangerous against allies who do not wield magical weapons or cast spells.

entries.name: Alioramus
entries.content:
Alioramus are sedulous hunters, their broad jaws capable of crushing a knight's chest through a full inch of iron plate.
Alioramus, which means "different branch", are a dinosaur beast found in the jungles of  Chult, often said to be one of the most dangerous places in Faerûn. They are recognisable by their colourful crests and, characteristic of theropods, three toes and claws on each limb.
Alioramus pounce on enemies, using their sharp teeth to bite and deal piercing damage. The alioramus colossa can also drive its pack into a 
Mating Frenzy.
They resemble a thorny velociraptor.

entries.name: Animated Armour
entries.content:
Suits of magically animated plate armour. Ponderous and persistent, these constructs are often used as guardians.
Animated armors are simply hollow suits of armor that patrol or guard often cursed by a wizard to eternally guard a thing.

entries.name: Automaton
entries.content:
Once a blueprint, now an indication of modern technology, this machine can only ever be a facsimile of a real person. Automatons are simple constructs, usually built to perform manual labour or to act as servants or butlers. They are powered by reserves of magical energy that can last for hundreds of years, and they are often found as heirlooms of noble houses or royalty.
They are often robotic looking in nature, tall and lanky and made completely of metal.

entries.name: Azer
entries.content:
Master craftsmen and expert miners made from bronze and fire.
Azer have the appearance of a dwarf made of bronze with hair and a bear of flame, they are often summoned in place of fire elementals by wizards or sorcerers.

entries.name: Blink Dog
entries.content:
The flickering, unpredictable magic of the faerie realm courses through the blink dog - allowing it to flit in and out of this plane to avoid harm.
Blink dogs are quite fast, and possess the ability to Blink(Teleport). For a canine, they possess an unusually muscular physique as well as large ears with green fur.

entries.name: Bulette
entries.content: The bulette's deep burrowing and powerful leap makes it an apex predator in nearly every terrain it finds itself in. Bulettes are extremely dangerous monstrosities. Their natural armour consists of thick plates layered across their bodies. Bulettes are typically native to hill environments but can be found in many different locations. Bulettes are sometimes referred to as Landsharks. They are very territorial and very aggressive when their territory is invaded

entries.name: Cloaker
entries.content: Resembling dark leathery cloaks, these aberrations lurk in caves, waiting to slay lone or injured prey stumbling through the darkness. Cloakers are large, permanently flying creatures that resemble large manta rays. They are often camouflaged when still, resembling a large cloak. They are aggressive stalking predators.

entries.name: Crawling Claw
entries.content:
Severed from their owners and skittering along on digits still stiff with rigor mortis, these hands can squeeze the breath from a throat in an instant.
Crawling claws are the reanimated amputated hands of humanoids. They are often crafted by necromancers to perform menial tasks, or employed as familiars by warlocks and wizards.

Crawling claws do not have a great deal of health or significant attacks, instead overwhelming their foes in swarms known as "applauses".

entries.name: Death Knight
entries.content:
When a fallen paladin dies without atonement, it can be brought back from the grave as something entirely different - entirely evil.
Death Knights appear fully clad in armour, such that you cannot see anything beneath.

entries.name: Death Shepherd
entries.content: Death Shepards are undead creatures that tend to a flock of lesser undead - such as zombies and ghouls. They are tall skeletons clad in armor that possess necromancy to resurrect any ghouls that may die in battle making them a dangerous foe of attrition.

entries.name: Deep Rothé
entries.content: Deep Rothé are common beasts in Faerûn, mostly used as a beef breed and beasts of burden. They are a sub-species of common Rothés, adapted to live in the Underdark. Rothé much resemble herd beasts like musk-oxen or yacks in appearance and probably share similar their temperament and behaviour.

entries.name: Displacer beast
entries.content:
A displacer beast's coat is slick with illusory magic that can bend light, letting it project images of itself and turn invisible. Adventurers say you can never know a displacer beast's true location - until its claws sink into your belly, that is. Displacer beasts are feline, tentacled creatures resembling panthers. They often live in small groups, preferring sheltered habitats such as caves or tree hollows.
Displacer beasts can be spoken to using 
Speak with Animals.

entries.name: Doppelganger
entries.content: Capable of morphing their physiology to impersonate other humanoids, doppelgangers have served as cunning spies, political envoys, and assassins. Doppelgangers can completely transform their appearance to mimic almost any Humanoid creature. They refer to themselves as Shallar. They will disguise themselves as other humanoids, then try to Ambush enemies by reverting to their true form.

entries.name: Elemental(s)
entries.content:
Elementals are creatures made of pure elements that are often summoned by a magic user in order to serve them often times in combat.
They can come multiple elements such as air, fire, earth, ice, lightning and grease.

entries.name: Ettercap
entries.content:
Though they only have two arms and two legs, these foul predators have more in common with the spiders they herd than with humanoids.
Ettercaps are humanoid spiders - unlike Driders these creatures appear more like spider abominations with arms, they often guards large spider nest.

entries.name: Flesh Golem
entries.content: The powerful enchantments that have stitched together this assortment of body parts have imbued it with both a strong defense and formidable strength. Flesh Golems are a type of construct built from a wide variety of fleshy body parts from once-living creatures. They are usually extremely strong and durable, though very quiet and obey their master. During a long fight, they can sometimes go berserk and attack everyone including it's master.

entries.name: Ghast
entries.content:
Orcus, god of undeath, creates ghasts by infusing ghouls with a particularly baleful dosage of his abyssal energy. Whereas a ghoul is little more than a savage beast, a ghast is cunning and can inspire a pack of ghouls to obey its commands.
Ghasts are similar to Ghouls – sharing a hunched, lean appearance and paralyzing claw attack – though larger, stronger, and permanently bearing an aura that resists being turned. They also have the unique ability to weaponize their stench and cause nausea in foes.

entries.name: Ghost
entries.content: The soul of a once-living creature, bound to the material plane by its desire to resolve some unfinished task from its life. Ghosts are a spectral form of undead.

entries.name: Ghoul
entries.content: Driven by their insatiable hunger for humanoid flesh, ghouls usually roam the night in packs. Ghouls devour the flesh of corpses and hunger for that of the living. Their claws can cause paralysis, and they are immune to Poison.

entries.name: Giant Eagle
entries.content: these creatures are simply very large eagles that are roughly the size of cows or larger.

entries.name: Gnoll
entries.content:
Feral, hyena-like humanoids that slaughter indiscriminately in an attempt to quell the insatiable hunger of their demonic creator, Yeenoghu.
Gnolls are a race of carnivorous humanoids, tall and lean with a craving for the hunt. They have a strong affinity for family and blood ties, though this comradery is not always extended to separate packs. Gnolls are fond of hyenas, viewing them as brethren and keeping them as pets or hunting companions. Gnolls can be born from bloated hyenas that are fat off the spoils of a massacre.

entries.name: Gremishka
entries.content:
The vicious product of spells gone wrong, these cat-like creatures delight in tormenting magic-users, relishing in the unstable effect magic has on them.
Gremishkas somewhat resemble a fur-less feline with the ears of a bat, and razor-sharp teeth.

entries.name: Hellsboar
entries.content:
Grafted with infernal iron and burning with hellfire, these porcine brutes are filled with a distinct brand of malice.
These boars are local to the realm of the hells as attack beast often sent in droves alongside imps.

entries.name: Hook Horror
entries.content:
Vulture-like, with a chitinous exoskeleton, the Hook Horror is a bipedal subterranean creature with razor-sharp hooks instead of hands.
They are terrifying ambush predators that often hang off the side of the cliffs in the underdark in order to ambush and slaughter their prey.

entries.name: Imp(s)
entries.content:
Cackling peddlers of infernal mischief, imps bind themselves to the service of more powerful devils who furnish them with commands.
These Fiends are often found in the hells as the one of the lowest in the demonic chain, they resemble something like a small, red skinned flying hairless monkey.

entries.name: Intellect Devourer
entries.content: Intellect devourers resemble glistening brains with four short clawed legs. They are drawn to, and feed on, Intelligence. Illithids breed intellect devourers by transforming the brain of a thrall. The subjected brain grows legs and becomes independent of its original body.

entries.name: Maazel
entries.content:
Twisted, cruel hermits affected by the Shadowfell. Imbued with magic, they move through the shadows to snatch their victims.
They are human sized creatures that use the shadows to their advantage in order to catch victims off guard and most likely consume them.

entries.name: Meenlock
entries.content: These crustacean-like Fey are spawned by fear and seek to destroy all that is good, innocent, and beautiful.

entries.name: Mephit
entries.content:
Capricious, vulgar, and rarely endearing - except to their masters. Mephits are curious, impish creatures from the Elemental Planes.
These creatures look much like Imps but they have larger and sharper noses and can be summoned much like an elemental.

entries.name: Merregon
entries.content:
In life, these faceless legionnaires of the Nine Hells were soldiers who served evil without reservation.
Merregon are faceless warriors, and permanently wear a mask and do not speak, instead communicating telepathically. They can be outfitted in a variety of armor and weapons but typically wield a halberd.

entries.name: Mimic
entries.content: Mimics can transform to take on the appearance of ordinary objects, often resembling that of treasure chests. They lie in wait and grow long tentacles and reveal sharp teeth, feasting on unaware prey that get close.

entries.name: Myrmidon
entries.content:
Myrmidons are elementals bound in armour. They have immunity to poison, and resistance to slashing, piercing and bludgeoning damage. Myrmidons are Permanently Armed, and as such cannot be disarmed. Air, fire and water myrmidons are also Ethereal so they cannot be shoved, thrown or used as an Improvised Melee Weapon.
Myrmidons can be transformed into by druids, or summoned by wizards, bards and druids

entries.name: Owlbear
entries.content: Resembling large feathered bears with the head of an owl, they are quick to anger, extremely strong and seemingly constantly hungry.  Their cubs are quite cute and can be domesticated.

entries.name: Phase spider
entries.content:
Giant spiders that can phase in and out of the Ethereal Plane, making it seem like they can teleport.
Phase spiders are arachnid-kin who dwell in the ethereal plane.

entries.name: Dragons
entries.content:
Immensely intelligent, ancient, and powerful reptiles that covet wealth.

Chromatic dragons are selfish, evil, and feared, while metallic dragons are noble, good, and respected by the wise.

entries.name: Scrying Eye
entries.content:
These levitating eyes transmit all that they see to the one who created them.
Scrying Eyes observe the actions of others and relay them to the secret leaders of the Cult of the Absolute. They can report crimes and attempt to alert their allies, if they are attacked. Scrying Eyes can be found at outposts of the Absolute.

entries.name: Shadow mastiff
entries.content:
Often moving as a pack, these hounds of the Shadowfell slink from shadow to shadow, always on the hunt.
They appear as large dogs and can disappear in the dark and only appear re-appear back in the light.

entries.name: Skeleton
entries.content: The remains of the dead, animated by dark magic - be they summoned by spellcasters, or risen on their own. Skeletons are the most basic and spare of undeadkind, all flesh and semblance of life stripped away from the body until only a chattering mockery remains. Being composed purely of brittle bone, all skeletons are vulnerable to Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Spectator
entries.content: Aggressive and greedy aberrations that believe their own forms to be the ideal, and hold all others - be it other beholders or 'lesser beings' - in contempt. Spectators are a lesser type of Beholder. They are floating creatures with a single huge eye and four eyestalks from which they may cast damaging or debilitating ray attacks.

entries.name: Steel Watcher
entries.content:
The operations of these huge steel juggernauts are powered by engines of churning hellfire.
Created by Enver Gortash to serve him, Steel Watchers uphold the law in the city of Baldur's Gate. Steel Watchers are formidable foes with large amounts of health.

entries.name: Worg
entries.content:
Vicious yet intelligent, these wolf-like creatures are often enslaved and trained by goblins to become savage warbeasts, guard dogs, trackers, and hunting companions.

Worgs are more sentient than the average animal and are capable of rudimentary speech without the need for Speak with Animals. They are not considered especially intelligent, however. Similarly to goblins, worgs are rude to all races but drow, who they identify as their "master's master." They're from the Nordiland worgata family.

entries.name: Wraith
entries.content:
A wraith is malice incarnate, concentrated into an incorporeal form that seeks to quench all life. Even small fires can be extinguished by the sucking oblivion of the wraith's horrifying existence.
Wraiths resemble Shadows but are significantly stronger and easily distinguished by their piercing yellow eyes. These creatures generate an Aura of Vile Oblivion that snuffs out any light sources and imposes magical darkness within melee range.

entries.name: Barbarian
entries.content:
Barbarians use their martial prowess and primal rage to strengthen themselves and dominate enemies in combat. The strong embrace the wild that hides inside - keen instincts, primal physicality, and most of all, an unbridled, unquenchable rage.

The Barbarians are able to enter a rage where nothing can make them feel fear, nor can they be surprised, often cleaving through things blindly with nothing but brute strength.

entries.name: Bard
entries.content:
Bards are expert storytellers, artists, and performers. Bards channel their power through song, speech, or performance to cast Spells. Bards know music is more than idle fancy - it is power. Through study and adventure, these travelling troubadours master song, speech, and the magic within.

Bards can be many things, promiscuous heart breakers to sword dancers that can write their own legendary songs when they retire.

entries.name: Cleric
entries.content:
Clerics worship and enact their deities' will to the world, for better or worse. They channel the power of their faith to cast Spells. Clerics are representatives of the gods they worship, wielding potent divine magic for good or ill.

Clerics are often times healers, Zealots blessed by their Deities to carry out their will.

entries.name: Druid
entries.content:
Druids are closely attuned with nature and the animals that live in it. They utilize the power of nature to cast Spells and have the ability to transform into various creatures. Druids channel the elemental forces of nature and share a deep kinship with animals. Mastery of Wild Shape allows them to transform into beasts from all over the Realms.

Often preferring the company of nature than people, Druids are guardians of the forest, often having...odd personalities and views compared to the rest of society.

entries.name: Fighter
entries.content:
Fighters use their martial expertise to fight enemies and support their allies in combat. Fighters have mastered the art of combat, wielding weapons with unmatched skill and wearing armour like a second skin.

Fighters are your average knight in shining armor, welding weapons like natural limbs, being able to don any armor, no matter it's weight and still fighting with ease in it. They are basic and magicless, but they should be feared, for a master fighter can slay the strongest of mages.

entries.name: Monk
entries.content:
Monks are unarmed combatants capable of spending Ki Points to perform special abilities. Some reach enlightenment by languid meditation - others do so in the heat of battle. Monks manipulate ki to empower their own strikes and debilitate their foes.

Monks have mastered their inner self to the maximum, their entire body often trained to be a living weapon. Fist like steel and a body as strong as dragon scales, A monk that has mastered their Ki is a force to be reckoned with.

entries.name: Paladin
entries.content:
Paladins are masters of a variety of weapons and armour. They channel the power of their sacred oath to heal the sick and injured and to smite their foes. A promise made so deeply that it becomes divine in itself flows through a paladin, burning bright enough to inspire allies and smite foes.

Paladins are people's who faith in something is so strong they are blessed by it with powers that can make the strongest of devils shutter, Often smiting down their foes and healing their comrades, beware a zealous paladin.

entries.name: Paladin (Oathbreaker)
entries.content:
Oathbreaker are what remains of a Paladin when they turn their back on their vow. These Paladins draw power from the darkness within to destroy their foes. "You have broken your sacred Oath in pursuit of power and ambition. Only darkness remains to fuel you now." - the first Oathbreaker knight.

These Oathbreakers are feared by society, seen as untrust worthy due to betraying their vow. They are the antithesis of a Paladin, often oozing necrotic magics and control of the shadows to rot and consume their enemies, All living things should learn to fear an Oathbreaker.

entries.name: Ranger
entries.content:
In tune with nature and their surroundings, Rangers utilize both their knowledge of the wilds and spellcasting to pursue their prey. Rangers are unrivalled scouts and trackers, honing a deep connection with nature in order to hunt their favoured prey. 

Rangers are swift, stealthy and deadly at a long range, often times a skilled ranger is never seen before their prey falls, swift as they are lethal, Be sure you're not the prey of a ranger.

entries.name: Rogue
entries.content:
Rogues are well versed in the art of stealth and rely on their resourcefulness to be in control of any challenging situation. With stealth, skill, and uncanny reflexes, rogues' versatility lets them get the upper hand in almost any situation.

Rogues are the thieves, the assassins, the cloak and daggers of society, they can be dangerous just as they are cunning, Oft times many people never detect a skilled rogue, not until the rogue chooses to make themselves known.

entries.name: Sorcerer
entries.content:
Sorcerers use their innate magical powers to fight enemies and aid allies in combat. Sorcerers are natural spellcasters, drawing on inherent magic from a gift or bloodline

Sorcerers are naturally gifted spellcasters due to their descendants often being that of a mighty dragon or a conniving fey, No matter it's fight ancestor, they can manipulate the weave in ways that wizards can only hope to, while they might not be able to be as versatile as  a wizard, their raw power  and mastery makes up for it.

entries.name: Warlock
entries.content:
Warlocks channel their patron's pact magic to fight enemies and aid allies in combat. Bound by a pact to an all-powerful patron, warlocks trade their loyalty for supernatural abilities and unique magic.

Often times magicless beings are visited by beings chaotic and evil or orderly and divine, ranging from unspeakable eldritch gods, Fiends, or Chaotic Fey's, Or even Angelic creatures like the Deva or Aasimir, at the price of their soul and freedom, they can obtain the power of those beings to rain down on their enemies.

entries.name: Wizard
entries.content:
Wizards channel magic through their extensive knowledge of the arcane to fight enemies and aid allies in combat. Wizards master the arcane by specializing in individual schools of magic, combining ancient spells with modern research.

Wizards are tamers and researchers of the Weave of magic, some for silly children's entertainment to spells that can exact unspeakable things onto their enemies, the one thing that all wizards have in common are their intelligence and their terrifying potential, Never earn a wizard's wrath...for it may be the last time you breath.

entries.name: Bahamut
entries.content:
The dragon god of justice, lawful good, Associated domain(s): Life, War.

The Angel of the Seven Heavens is the dragon god of justice. His ideal of mercy and just authority keep him locked in an inexorable rivalry with his sister, Tiamat.

entries.name: Bane
entries.content:
The god of tyranny, terror and hate, lawful evil. Associated domain(s): Order, War.

Bane is a dark paragon of hate, fear, and tyranny. He ascended to godhood alongside Bhaal and Myrkul, but loathes them both for taking power he believes is rightfully his.

entries.name: Bhaal
entries.content:
The god of murder, neutral evil. Associated domain(s): Death.

Bhaal is the notorious god of murder, reborn after each of his descendants were viciously slain. He has a tenuous alliance with Myrkul and Bane, the three having attained divinity in a bargain with the fallen god Jergal.

entries.name: Corellon Larethian
entries.content:
The elf god of art and magic, chaotic good. Associated domain(s): Arcana, Life, Light, War.

Creator of the elves, Corellon Larethian oversees the elven pantheon as a whole, providing blessings to those who study art, magic, and nature.

entries.name: Cyric
entries.content:
The god of lies, trickery, and strife, chaotic evil. Associated domain(s): Trickery.

Known as the Prince of Lies, Cyric previously held dominion over tyranny, murder, lies, intrigue, and illusion. He has a storied rivalry with Mystra.

entries.name: Eilistraee
entries.content:
The drow goddess of beauty and freedom, chaotic good. Associated domain(s): Life, Light, Nature

Eilistraee is the goddess of good-aligned drow, beauty, song, and freedom. The Dark Maiden desires balance between all races, and struggles against her mother Lolth's corrupt aims.

entries.name: Garl Glittergold
entries.content:
The gnome god of luck, protection and trickery, lawful good. Associated domain(s): Trickery.

The Watchful Protector is the king of gnomish gods - a deity of humour, gemcutting, protection, and trickery.

entries.name: Gond
entries.content:
The god of craft, smithing, and inventiveness. Neutral (as Gond), chaotic good (as Nebelun). Associated domain(s): Forge (as Gond), Knowledge, Trickery (as Nebelun)

The Lord of All Smiths had many forms and names, and under all of them pushed for innovation and imaginativeness, sometimes to a dangerous degree, as a result of his short-sighted desire to create. Gond was also known as Nebelun among Gnomes of the Realms, who venerated him alongside the other Lords of the Golden Hills (the Gnome pantheon).

entries.name: Gruumsh
entries.content:
The patron deity of orcs and head of the orc pantheon, chaotic evil. Associated domain(s): Tempest, War.

The One-Eye is the orcs' patron deity - a god of war, conquest, and victory at all costs. He has led an ancient and immutable grudge against the elven pantheon since Corellon Larethian took his eye.

entries.name: Helm
entries.content:
The god of protection and guardians, lawful neutral. Associated domain(s): Life, Light, Twilight.

The Watcher is an eternal sentry among the gods, representing guardians across the planes. After more than a century of fading worship, Helm's power was restored with the Second Sundering.

entries.name: Ilmater
entries.content:
The god of endurance and suffering, lawful good. Associated domain(s): Life, Twilight.

The Crying God protects the oppressed and persecuted. His clergy is sworn to alleviate suffering, even if that means taking on that pain personally.

entries.name: Jergal
entries.content:
The Final Scribe, formerly Lord of Bones, Judge of the Damned. Lawful neutral. Associated domain(s): Death, Knowledge.

The original god of death before he willingly ceded his position to Bhaal, Bane, and Myrkul who usurped some of his portfolios. After stepping down he became the seneschal of first Myrkul, then Cyric (after Myrkul perished during the Times of Troubles), and eventually Kelemvor (after Cyric was overthrown by Mystra and Kelemvor).

Caring for little besides an orderly accounting of the fate of the world, Jergal became known as the Final Scribe who kept the records of the ultimate fate of all the dead.

entries.name: Kelemvor
entries.content:
The god of the dead, lawful neutral. Associated domain(s): Death, Grave.

Fair but distant, Kelemvor guides the dead to their appropriate plane in the afterlife. His clergy provides last rites across Faerûn, but also destroy undead that have escaped Kelemvor's judgement.

entries.name: Kereska
entries.content:
The dragon goddess of magic and magical creativity, chaotic neutral. Associated domain(s): Arcana.

Kereska, draconic goddess of arcane knowledge, imbues many chromatic dragons with their magic, including their breath.

entries.name: Laduguer
entries.content:
Laduguer 'The Exile' is the tyrannical patron of the Duergar, lawful evil. Associated domain(s): Arcana, Death.

His clerics are the unquestioned rulers of duergar society, enforcing cold and callous behaviour among his worshippers.

entries.name: Lathander
entries.content:
The god of birth, dawn and renewal, neutral good. Associated domain(s): Life, Light.

The Morninglord is the god of the dawn and spring, of birth and beginnings. He is invoked to christen both new ventures and new life. His followers embrace growth and renewal, and despise the undead.

entries.name: Lolth
entries.content:
The drow goddess of spiders, chaotic evil. Associated domain(s): Trickery, War.

The much-reviled matriarch of the drow pantheon, Lolth holds sway over spiders, the Underdark, and the wicked creatures of the Demonweb Pits. Her primary goal is to corrupt all drow, transforming them into heartless cultists.

entries.name: Loviatar
entries.content:
Loviatar the evil goddess of agony, lawful evil. Associated domain(s): Death.

Queen and servant to the greater god Bane, the Maiden of Pain is the master of inflicting physical and psychological suffering, her portfolio encompassing hurt and torture. Abdirak is a notable servant of Loviatar.

entries.name: Mielikki
entries.content:
The goddess of forests, neutral good. Associated domain(s): Nature.

Mielikki is the goddess of forests and the creatures that live within them. She is a remote and spiritual deity, often spoken of in but the quietest of forests.

entries.name: Moradin
entries.content:
The dwarf god of creation, lawful good. Associated domain(s): Forge, Knowledge.

The All-Hammer is a dwarven god worshipped by smiths, artisans, and miners alike. He and Laduguer are constantly at odds.

entries.name: Myrkul
entries.content:
The god of death and decay, neutral evil. Associated domain(s): Death.

A member of the Dead Three with Bhaal and Bane, Myrkul is a cruel necromancer turned god, inspiring the fear of death in mortals. He often clashes with Kelemvor, the even-handed judge of fallen souls.

entries.name: Mystra
entries.content:
The goddess of magic, neutral good. Associated domain(s): Arcana, Knowledge.

As the mother of all magic, Mystra oversees the Weave and spreads arcane knowledge to mortal spellcasters. Her clerics preserve ancient lore and protect bastions of magical energy.

entries.name: Oghma
entries.content:
The god of knowledge, neutral. Associated domain(s): Knowledge.

Oghma is the god of inspiration and invention, sharing knowledge with the world through his bards and clerics. Unlike many other deities, Oghma accepts all moral alignments into his clergy.

entries.name: Selûne
entries.content:
The goddess of the moon, chaotic good. Associated domain(s): Knowledge, Life, Twilight.

The Lady of Silver presides over the moon, stars, and navigation. Her power over the heavens is constantly challenged by her sister Shar, who seeks to plunge the world into eternal shadow.

entries.name: Shar
entries.content:
The goddess of darkness and loss, neutral evil. Associated domain(s): Death, Trickery.

As the greater deity of darkness, Shar is feared for her power over the night, secrets, and loss. She is locked in eternal conflict with her twin sister Selûne, goddess of the moon.

entries.name: Silvanus
entries.content:
The god of nature and wilderness, neutral. Associated domain(s): Nature.

Silvanus, known also as the Treefather or Oak Father, presides over nature, specifically wild nature, in both its natural beauty and fierce savagery. He can be wild and unpredictable, much like nature itself, and is wrathful towards those who threaten wild places. He is the patron of Druids.

entries.name: Talos
entries.content:
The god of storms and destruction, chaotic evil. Associated domain(s): Tempest.

Talos represents the uncaring and destructive force of nature. His followers see life as a set of random effects in a sea of chaos, and take what they can - for who can say when Talos will strike next?

entries.name: Tempus
entries.content:
The god of war, neutral. Associated domain(s): War.

Tempus is the Lord of Battles, overseeing war and its soldiers. He is the embodiment of honorable combat, and condemns needless bloodlust.

entries.name: Tiamat
entries.content:
The dragon goddess of greed, lawful evil and chaotic evil. Associated domain(s): Trickery.

Tiamat the Many-Mawed is a roiling mass of avarice and hate currently trapped within the Nine Hells. The dragon god of greed eternally plots her escape, as do her many fanatics in the world of Toril.

entries.name: Tymora
entries.content:
The goddess of good fortune, chaotic good. Associated domain(s): Trickery.

Tymora is the bright-faced goddess of fortune, who favours those who gamble - and set out on adventure - with the utmost skill and daring.

entries.name: Tyr
entries.content:
The god of law and justice, lawful good. Associated domain(s): Order, War.

The Blind God rules over law and justice, encouraging valiant acts from his followers and relentlessly pursuing oathbreakers.

entries.name: Umberlee
entries.content:
The Bitch Queen, Umberlee, is the sea goddess, chaotic evil. Associated domain(s): Tempest.

She is most often worshipped by sailors or people travelling by sea, out of fear of her destructive powers. The Queen of the Depths was known as a particularly malicious, petty, greedy, and vain deity who controlled the harshness of the sea while revelling in her own power and was not hesitant to drown people if she so pleased

entries.name: Vlaakith
entries.content: While not a god in the traditional sense, the Lich Queen is the sole respected leader of the githyanki. She encourages their worship and unquestioning devotion, essentially acting as a deity.

entries.name: Yondalla
entries.content:
The halfling goddess of fertility and protection. Lawful good. Associated domain(s): Life, Twilight.

As the mother of the halfling pantheon, Yondalla is known for her kindness and open mind, encouraging her followers to protect the home, hearth, and nature
